# Test directory listing functionality

# Change to test directory
cd testdir

# Start server in directory listing mode (no input file)
md2html -http :8092 &

# Wait for server
wait-port :8092

# A directory with an index file serves that file, not a listing
curl -s http://localhost:8092/
stdout '<h1.*>Welcome</h1>'
stdout '<title>Welcome</title>'
! stdout 'Index of'

# A directory without an index file serves a listing of its markdown files,
# named relative to the served root rather than by its location on disk
curl -s http://localhost:8092/subdir/
stdout 'Index of /subdir'
stdout 'nested\.md'

# A directory URL without a trailing slash redirects to one, so that the
# relative links in the listing resolve
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' http://localhost:8092/subdir
stdout '301 http://localhost:8092/subdir/'

# Test individual file access via clean URLs
curl -s http://localhost:8092/file1
stdout '<h1.*>File One</h1>'

# The page title comes from the first heading when there is no frontmatter
curl -s http://localhost:8092/file2
stdout '<h1.*>File Two</h1>'
stdout '<title>File Two</title>'

-- testdir/index.md --
# Welcome

This is the index page for testing directory listings.

-- testdir/file1.md --
# File One

This is the first test file.

-- testdir/file2.md --
# File Two

This is the second test file.

-- testdir/subdir/nested.md --
# Nested File

This file is in a subdirectory.
